structure: Part 9, commodity search and selection, in the live-animals linear journey's commodities feature. Read in full: every non-test file under features/commodities/search/ (search.controller.js with its GET, POST and POST commodities/results routes; search.njk; _results.njk, the shared results-and-chosen-panel macro; search-results.njk, the live-refresh fragment; search-query.js; test-support.js; actions/commit-selection.js; selection/keys.js, line-key.js, rows.js, remove-action.js, selected-keys.js; view-model/selected-summary.js, labels.js, commodity-groups.js, result-order.js), the feature-level page.js, evaluation.js, commodity-question-detour.js, lines.js, species-label.js, commodity-label.js, action-prefix.js, view-model/selected-commodity-rows.js and view-model/commodity-groups.js, copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (search keys claimed; selectedCommodities headings claimed as the table builder in this slice uses them; consignmentDetails and identification keys left to part 10), the feature-level test-support.js, and fit/search.fit.spec.js (all 9 describe blocks, 44 tests). Covered: one page, slug commodities (maturity detailing), with a search box, grouped tick-box results, a chosen-species panel with chips, Remove and Clear all, an Add selection fallback button, a commodity-code help section, three save controls and one validation error; the live results route used with JavaScript; how a selection is stored (flow-only commoditySearchRows) and committed as commodityLines; the commodity-question detour from the commodity details and animal identification pages; and how commodity lines are published. The earlier extract's claims for this slice were checked against today's files and all still hold, so every kept id is kept; new claims start at repo-frontend-p9-103.

export const normaliseQuery = (value) => String(value ?? '').trim()

export const isSearchable = (query) =>
  normaliseQuery(query).length >= MIN_SEARCH_LENGTH

Each result row offers one species, labelled with its Latin name and its common name in brackets, such as "Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle)", and with the Latin name alone when the list holds no common name for it.
A search matches a species by its common name as well as by its Latin name and by commodity code.
One species that sits under two commodity codes is listed once under each, as two separate choices.
The part of the commodity heading and of the species label that the search term matched is shown in bold, including a match inside the common name.

claims.statement: The species a search returned are held against the journey between page views under a flow-only answer named commoditySearchRows, which is replaced on each search and emptied once a selection is saved.
claims.quote:
export const STORED_SEARCH_ROWS = 'commoditySearchRows'
...
export const replaceStoredSearchRows = (request, h, rows) =>
  state.commit(request, h, {
    [STORED_SEARCH_ROWS]: [...rowsByKey(rows).values()]
  })

export const clearStoredSearchRows = (request, h) =>
  state.commit(request, h, { [STORED_SEARCH_ROWS]: [] })
claims.note: mechanism: holds each returned row's commodity code, Latin name and common name so a later post can resolve a chosen key.
